question: Do six matched KAE rows, with one learned refinement in every LISTA encoder, improve strict direct long-horizon forecasting on ten chaotic Dysts systems at verified dt times 30?
invalid_predecessors: Historical KAE caches used native dt while metadata claimed dt times 30; all historical Dysts outcomes are quarantined.
Replacement chain 10173424 was stopped before a valid optimizer step because GPU workers inherited the legacy cache root and the cache CLI omitted the policy split.

The v4 smoke completed all 12 corrected fits with 99--100 percent sustained GPU utilization, but its downstream gate falsely treated the unused GenericKM encoder-type default as an active LISTA encoder; the full chain was therefore blocked before launch.

In v5 cache job 10173636, 36 of 40 split caches completed, but the four Sakarya splits made no progress for 10--13 hours because individual strict-Radau integrations became pathological solver stragglers. Those four tasks were canceled after about 14 hours; dependent jobs 10173637 and 10173638 were canceled before allocation, so no GPU work was lost.
repairs: The native integrator receives the dt override and a ten-system numerical validator compares corrected points with native-grid subsampling.
Schema-3 train, validation, policy, and test caches use split-specific perturbed initial conditions and exact metadata, shape, dtype, count, and finiteness checks.
Every GPU worker receives the isolated cache path explicitly; the smoke gate verifies that path in every saved config.
LISTA, LISTA-BD, and LISTA-SB each use one learned S refinement; a unit test requires nonzero S gradients.
Dysts checkpoint selection uses held-out validation futures and direct repeated-K rollout, matching the primary endpoint.
Per-initial-condition survival and strict full-horizon metrics prevent finite prefixes from rewarding divergence.

The Sakarya-only restart preserves every deterministic split initial condition, corrected dt times 30 output grid, and 1e-12 tolerances. Every Sakarya trajectory uses DOP853; no wall-time-dependent mixed-solver fallback or initial-condition filtering is permitted, and the saved cache records the uniform solver count.

cache_restart.motivation: Uniform DOP853 removes machine-load-dependent solver assignment and does not consume the standardized analytic Jacobian used by Radau in Dysts 0.96.
cache_restart.smoke_gate: Passed: 32 of 32 finite trajectories, exact shape 32 by 5001 by 3, all 32 recorded as DOP853, 10.8 seconds cache-build time with four workers.

training.checkpoint_selection: direct repeated-K H200 on a disjoint native validation cache
training.dense_contract: tanh hidden activations, linear dense latent output, dense K, zero sparsity coefficient, no shrinkage, ReLU output gate, top-k, block penalty, or weight decay intended to induce zeros

evaluation.primary: direct repeated-K strict full-horizon MSE and survival
evaluation.secondary: fixed periodic cadences 25, 100, and 200; any test-set best-periodic envelope is exploratory
evaluation.statistics: summarize paired seeds within each system, then treat ten systems as independent units

compute.packing: 12 concurrent fits per GPU with 32 GiB host memory
compute.smoke_gate: exactly 12 Chua receipts; isolated cache path in every config; direct checkpoint selector in every checkpoint; finite metrics; mean GPU >=70%, active mean >=80%, peak >=95%

failure_policy: Any missing, stale, wrong-cache, wrong-depth, wrong-selector, nonfinite, incomplete, or provenance-mismatched row blocks downstream work. The selector may reject all models; no partial packet supports a claim.
